title: Demand-led quarterly roadmap: capacity threshold alignment and OKR mapping for hosted API + model catalog
creator: Oliver Grant
description: Quarterly plan to tie Hosted API model-catalog commitments to demand-driven capacity thresholds and explicit OKR milestones. Objective is to convert usage signals and backlog forecasts into deterministic commit lanes (reserved capacity + burst hedges), map each lane to outcome-oriented OKRs, and define operational triggers for canary windows, model rotation, and rollback policies. This ticket defines thresholds, milestone acceptance criteria, cross-team responsibilities, and playbook snippets to make the quarter executable and auditable.
milestones: M1: Commit lanes defined and approved by finance & infra (acceptance: lane cost model + 90-day forecast) - target 2026-03-01
M2: Instrumentation & dashboard with threshold alerts (acceptance: alert fire tests + ownership) - target 2026-03-18
M3: Canary scheduling and rollback playbook baked into release cadence (acceptance: dry-run canary) - target 2026-03-29
M4: OKR mapping finalized and communicated to GTM (acceptance: stakeholder sign-off) - target 2026-04-05
scenario_triggers: Baseline: sustained commit utilization < 60% -> standard release cadence, no extra capacity
Growth: commit utilization 60%-85% for 7 days -> trigger 'hedge' policy: reserve incremental burst nodes; notify Capacity Ops
Spike: commit utilization > 85% for 24 hours or 95th percentile latency breach -> activate emergency scale & model-fallback lane and escalate to on-call leads
Model quality regression: eval delta > 3% on golden prompt set -> pause automated rotations and open rollback incident runbook
canary_windows: Small canary (1% traffic) for 2 hours during low-traffic window: validate latency, cost, and quality metrics
Staged canary (10% traffic) for 12 hours with automated hold conditions on token-error-rate, highest-latency tail, and quality regression
Full rollout gated by 72-hour health window and manual sign-off from PM + SRE
decisions: Adopt three commit lanes: 'Baseline' (self-serve), 'Hedge' (reserved + burst), 'Emergency' (priority routing + fallbacks); approved by Finance on 2026-02-22
Use combined signal of utilization and latency tail for capacity triggers to avoid scaling on noisy single metrics
Map OKR-1 (reduce served-cost-per-1k tokens by 12%) to conservative batching + quantization experiments in the Hedge lane; OKR-2 (99.8% p99 latency) mapped to routing and fallback SLOs
